definition: Epitome means a perfect example or embodiment of a quality.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word epitome. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know epitome should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: With his pressed apron and pocket watch, the stationmaster was the epitome of old-railway courtesy.
An example is far weaker than the epitome — any single case will do to show the quality, while the epitome shows it at its purest, the case the others are judged against.
A model stops short of the epitome — worth copying, yet still improvable; the epitome is the quality made flesh, with nothing left to add.

Embodiment is the near-twin: a quality given a body, patience walking around in shoes. The epitome adds a ranking — it is not just the quality made visible but the case every other is measured against. Every epitome is an embodiment; only the best embodiment is the epitome.

An exemplar is the model case held up for imitation — cooler, more instructional, a teaching specimen. The epitome is praise with a superlative built in: it shows the quality at its purest, whether or not anyone could hope to copy it. An exemplar instructs; the epitome crowns.

A- means not, so the Greeks named the atom the thing that cannot be cut any smaller — the same tom- blade at work.
Epitome means a perfect example or embodiment of a quality.
In the knife maker's workshop hang a hundred blades, but apprentices are marched past all of them to one plain chef's knife on a black peg — the epitome of the craft.
Nothing about it shouts: the handle is unadorned, the steel unpolished past what work requires.
Yet balance, edge, and temper meet in it so completely that the master simply calls it the lesson.
Epitome is the exact word for that knife, because epitome means a perfect example or embodiment of a quality — the whole idea of the craft, compressed into one object.
Any blade on the wall is an example; the epitome is the example the others are judged against, the case that shows the quality at its purest.
Epitome is praise with a superlative built in: call someone the epitome of patience and you rank them, not just describe them.
Embodiment is the near-twin without the ranking; exemplar is cooler and more instructional.
Paradigm, met among this unit's reference words, is different furniture — a pattern others follow, not a quality made flesh.
And note the fixed frame: always the epitome of something.

Design students meet the 1933 harbor-city subway map in their first week, and most never stop talking about it.
Other maps came earlier, and hundreds came after, but this one is still called the epitome of clean wayfinding: every later designer is measured against it, fairly or not.
Its maker broke the rules of geography on purpose, spacing the stations evenly and bending the river into a polite curve so the eye could travel without stumbling.
Plenty of transit maps are clear, and committees have produced tidy, workable diagrams for a century.
But when critics want to name the standard itself — the case the whole craft is judged by — they reach for this one map, and the argument usually ends there.
